history.administration_response: The United Nations occupational safety and health management system was introduced through the promulgation of Secretary-General’s bulletin ST/SGB/2018/5, in which he indicated that the system would be implemented in a phased manner. The Administration stated that an occupational safety and health management system required multiple components for which personnel resourcing had not been made available. Therefore, the full implementation of this recommendation was subject to the availability of resources from Member States.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration establish a United Nations occupational safety and health management system that also includes COVID-19 measures.
history.administration_response: The Administration stated that the recommendation is under implementation. The workforce review regarding additional resources provided in February 2022 was completed, but no further progress was made. Therefore, a wider strategic review of implementation of the occupational safety and health management system took place that narrowed the scope of introduction of an occupational safety and health management system to those locations with a professional safety officer to perform key occupational safety and health functions. This revised process is under way, with the first major component (incident reporting system) to be established in missions that meet the criteria by the end of December 2022.
history.board_assessment: The Administration has taken an additional step towards the implementation of the recommendation (workforce review). The Board considers this recommendation as under implementation.

The incident reporting technological solution has been revised and upgraded to include COVID-19 reporting.
history.board_assessment: Work is still ongoing. The Board considers the recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration establish a United Nations occupational safety and health management system that also includes coronavirus disease (COVID-19) measures.
history.administration_response: The occupational safety and health management system is progressively implemented at United Nations Headquarters and those locations that have a professional safety officer to perform key occupational safety and health functions. Given that most missions have no safety personnel, further initiatives are under way to staff this function with a qualified safety officer. This remains the key barrier to the establishment of an occupational safety and health capability. The occupational safety and health management system continues to be adapted to align with wider organizational and High-level Committee on Management guidance. Further progress includes the publishing of the fundamentals of occupational safety and health course for all staff. The incident reporting technological solution includes COVID-19 and is being adapted to better integrate compensation claims. The Board is requested to consider the efforts taken to implement the recommendation and close it.
history.board_assessment: The Administration has been implementing an occupational safety and health management system that covers the issues raised in the recommendation. Specific training was launched in September 2024. The recommendation is considered implemented.
